summary: Somerset County tower: a 1910 wood lookout replaced in 1914 by a 24-ft steel tower; the FFLA lists it standing without its cab, which a 2021 trip report confirms.

facts.design: 24-ft steel tower with an 8x8x7 ft cab, built in 1914 to replace a 1910 wood tower
facts.status_note: The steel tower still stands, but its cab is gone (FFLA; a 2021 trip report agrees)

visit.trail_note: A 2021 trip report describes a road on the north slope that gets about a mile from the summit, then a bushwhack with no trail to the tower

events.note: Wood lookout tower on the summit, per Maine Memory and the Maine Historical Society photo inventory
A 24-ft steel tower with an 8x8 cab replaced the 1910 wood tower
A new telephone line ran from company camps to the top of Tumbledown, per the 1914 Forest Commissioner's report
Fire watchman camp on Tumbledown, photographed in 1915; the watchman's note describes it
Tower painted, per the 1916 Forest Commissioner's report

notes_for_editor: Dates and dimensions agree between Maine Memory and the Eastern US Lookouts page. The cab removal date is unknown; the only condition evidence is the FFLA note and a 2021 trip report. No current owner, access rule or condition report was found, and the trip report describes a bushwhack, so the story does not encourage a climb. The 1915 'staffed' event rests on a photo caption and the watchman's note, not on a staffing record. A Forest Fire Lookout Association Maine post says the tower has not really been manned since the 1930s, but I did not read that post, so it is not used.
